blackout_config_invalid.description: A host blackout entry (scheduling.blackout.host) breaks a rule; field points at the member, blackout_id names the entry when it has one. check-config and startup refuse the configuration.
blackout_config_invalid.common_causes: A duplicate id, a weekday outside 1 to 7, a minute of day outside 0 to 1439, or an offset outside the allowed range.
blackout_config_invalid.handling: Fix the entry and commit the configuration again.

config_key_not_settable.description: A ConfigureSettings change names a key the Runtime reads only at start; it cannot change while the Runtime runs, and the whole request is refused.
config_key_not_settable.common_causes: The key is read before the ledger opens or once by the start-up assembly.
config_key_not_settable.handling: Change the key in the configuration file, commit it with acsetup and restart the daemon.

config_key_unknown.description: A ConfigureSettings change names a key the configuration key table does not have, or a per-instance key of an instance that is not configured; the whole request is refused and nothing changes.
config_key_unknown.common_causes: A misspelt key, a key of a later Runtime, or an instance id that is not in the configuration.
config_key_unknown.handling: Read the keys in effect with actingctl status --config and send the change again with an existing key.

config_override_base_changed.description: At start an instruction value was kept although the default it overrode changed in this Runtime release; the file still does not name the key.
config_override_base_changed.common_causes: A new Runtime release changed the key's default.
config_override_base_changed.handling: Check whether the instruction value is still wanted; clear it to take the new default.

config_override_dropped.description: At start an instruction value was dropped because its key no longer exists, can no longer change while the Runtime runs, or its value no longer fits the key.
config_override_dropped.common_causes: The instance was removed from the configuration, or a Runtime release changed the key.
config_override_dropped.handling: Set the key again by instruction if it still applies.

config_override_superseded.description: At start an instruction value was dropped: the configuration file changed or removed the value it overrode, or now names a key whose default it overrode. The later change wins.
config_override_superseded.common_causes: The configuration file was edited and committed after the setting was changed by instruction.
config_override_superseded.handling: Nothing to repair; set the key by instruction again if the file value is not wanted.

config_value_invalid.description: A ConfigureSettings change carries a value of the wrong type or outside the key's range, names the same key twice, or leaves its section failing the section's whole-section check (config_value_problem says which); the whole request is refused and nothing changes.
config_value_invalid.common_causes: A value of another JSON type, a number outside range_min..range_max, or a combination the section does not allow.
config_value_invalid.handling: Send the change again with a value of the key's type and range.

recovery_ladder_code_unclassified.description: The recovery ladder met a code the embedded catalog does not list and read it as ladder class none (raw_code is its spelling); recorded once per process and code. No trigger item matches it by class.
recovery_ladder_code_unclassified.common_causes: A code a newer component emits that this build's catalog does not list yet.
recovery_ladder_code_unclassified.handling: Update the Runtime; to start a ladder on the code, list it in a trigger item's codes once the catalog has it.

recovery_ladder_config_invalid.description: The recovery_ladder section breaks a rule of its whole-section check (config_key names the key, config_value_problem the rule); startup and check-config refuse the configuration. The same values sent by a ConfigureSettings instruction are refused as config_value_invalid with the same key and problem, and the Runtime keeps its configuration.
recovery_ladder_config_invalid.common_causes: Two trigger items with one id, a stage no item may name, a code or class the catalog does not list, count and window_ms on the wrong item, a start rung beyond the rungs, a rung bound below the device layer's, or a claim TTL or bound beyond the longest renewal.
recovery_ladder_config_invalid.handling: Fix the key config_key names as config_value_problem says, then commit the configuration again.
